name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with system preference as the default dark mode, but add a persistent toggle in the top-right corner. Dark themes reduce eye strain in low light and improve readability for dense data—matching the competitive analysis and Graphify’s proven user preference. The toggle respects user choice without forcing a manual override each session. Trade-off: a slight increase in initial interface clutter, but the clarity and enjoyment gains outweigh it.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Defaulting to system preference still risks users who prefer light mode in bright environments—dark mode degrades readability for dense data in daylight. A persistent toggle solves nothing if users never notice it. Ship EXCAVA with a *one-time* mode selector at first launch instead; track toggle usage for 30 days, then decide.

name: Facet
text:
Ship EXCAVA with a one-time mode selector at first launch, defaulting to system preference but letting users pick light or dark mode once and for all. This cuts the risk of users missing the toggle while still respecting their preference—dark mode for low light, light mode for daylight readability. The trade-off is a single extra click at first launch, but it avoids the bigger risk of users stuck in the wrong mode.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A one-time selector still locks users into a choice they may regret—what if their environment changes? A persistent toggle with a clear affordance (like a high-contrast icon) is the only way to avoid forcing users to live with a bad default. Settle it with A/B testing: measure drop-off rates between the two approaches over two weeks.
